newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals futures end up on weaker yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals futures end up on weaker yen.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures closed higher on Wednesday as the yen's falls against the dollar triggered active buying by individual investors, traders said.
Platinum futures ended nine to 44 yen higher, with the benchmark June 1998 contract up 38 yen 1,345 yen per gram.
"The yen's falls and concern about Russian metal supply accelerated buying orders," a brokerage house trader said.
Although Russia has resumed its platinum group metal (PGM) exports for this year, Japanese investors are worried about the stability of Russian supplies next year, traders said.
A power struggle among Russian entities for control over multi-billion-dollar exports is intensifying, despite Russia's resumption of supplies to Japan, sources in Moscow said.
"It's better to assume that metal exports from Russia could be unstable at any time," a platinum trader in Tokyo said.
Palladium futures ended three yen lower to seven yen higher, with benchmark June up seven yen at 522 yen per gram.

Gold futures were higher across the board at the close, supported by the yen's weaker tone, traders said. The June was up seven yen at 1,167 yen per gram. Bullion was traded at $318.80/319.90 at 0750 GMT, against $318.00/50 in New York.
